I could see the strains of hardship on the faces of the Muslims and I could also notice the happiness on the faces of the Munaafiqeen (who were happy to see the Muslims suffer). When Rasulullaah ﷺ noticed this, he said, 'Allaah shall provide sustenance before the sun sets.' Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) knew that the words of Allaah and His Rasool ﷺ were always true, so he bought fourteen camels together with the loads of food they carried. He then sent nine to Rasulullaah ﷺ. When Rasulullaah ﷺ saw them, he asked, 'What are these?' 'They are a gift to you from Uthmaan,' came the reply. The happiness on the face of Rasulullaah ﷺ was then clearly noticeable, while the faces of the Munaafiqeen displayed only unhappiness. I then saw Rasulullaah ﷺ raise his hands so high to pray for Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) that I could even the see the whiteness of his armpits. He made such du'aa for Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) that I had never before or ever after heard him make for anyone else. He prayed for Allaah to reward Hadhrat Uthmaan (RA) abundantly and to treat him every so graciously."[^1]
The Statement of Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) Concerning the Virtues of Giving Gifts

Hadhrat Abdullaah bin Abbaas (RA) once stated, "For me to fulfil the necessities of a Muslim family for a month or for a week or for whatever period of time Allaah pleases is more beloved to me than performing Hajj after Hajj. Buying a utensil for even a Daaniq (one-sixth of a Dirham) and giving it to my brother as a gift for the pleasure of Allaah is more beloved to me than spending a Dinaar in the path of Allaah."[^2]
The Statement of Hadhrat Ali (RA) About the Virtue of Feeding Others
Hadhrat Ali (RA) once mentioned, "To gather a few of my friends to share a Saa of food is more beloved to me than proceeding to the marketplace to purchase a slave and set him free."[^3]
The Narration of Hadhrat Jaabir (RA) in this Regard

Hadhrat Abdul Waahid bin Ayman reports from his father that when some guests came to Hadhrat Jaabir (RA), he brought some bread and vinegar for them and said, "Eat this because I have heard Rasulullaah ﷺ say that vinegar is an excellent gravy.
